error_detail.message_markdown:
**This Manual page isn't available**

`SMTO-MAN-0002` · `manual-document-not-found`

The Manual link you opened points to a page this version of the Manual doesn't have. It may be an old bookmark, a mistyped link, or a page that was renamed.

**How to fix**

1. Open Manual from the navigation menu and type the topic or error code into the Search manual box. Search only lists pages this version actually contains, so it finds the page under its current name.
2. If you came from an error message, go back to it and select Explain this error again. The error panel builds a fresh link to that error's current Manual page.
3. If pages for error codes are missing but other pages open, tell the person who manages SMTO. Error-code pages are built when the Manual starts, and if that step failed only those pages are missing.

**What success looks like**

The Manual shows the page's title and text instead of the error.

**If it still fails**

Copy the link you opened and the error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Replace any old bookmark with the link you get from search.

**Technical details**

The Manual service returned 404 because the validated document ID has no entry in the current corpus snapshot (a stale or mistyped link, a removed or renamed document, or generated reference pages that were not published).

Check the ID against GET /api/manual/catalog and the document count in /healthz. If generated pages such as error-smto-* are missing, check the Manual service log for a failed generated-reference build at startup (docs_generated_cache_failures); authored pages are still served.

error_detail.title: This Manual link isn't in a form SMTO recognizes
error_detail.short_description: Manual ID validation failed: the requested document ID is not 1-120 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens starting with a letter or digit (HTTP 400), or corpus construction rejected duplicate document IDs, an unknown authority, inconsistent source classification or headings, or duplicate section references.
error_detail.long_description: Manual ID validation rejects unsupported syntax, or corpus construction finds duplicate identities, inconsistent source authority/headings or duplicate section references. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
error_detail.explain_like_5: The page name in this Manual link uses characters or a length the Manual doesn't allow, so it couldn't look the page up. Nothing was changed.

how_to_fix.summary: For a 400 response, use a valid lowercase document ID from GET /api/manual/catalog. If corpus construction raised ValueError in manual.corpus._snapshot, repair or reinstall the installed Manual content so document IDs and section references are unique and front-matter headings match the document body.

steps.instruction: Use a current canonical link; if corpus construction reports conflicting document metadata, repair the installed Manual content.

steps.instruction: If every Manual page fails to open, tell the person who manages SMTO.
steps.why: A damaged Manual installation, for example two pages with the same name, stops the Manual from loading its pages.

error_detail.message_markdown:
**This Manual link isn't in a form SMTO recognizes**

`SMTO-MAN-0003` · `manual-document-invalid`

The page name in this Manual link uses characters or a length the Manual doesn't allow, so it couldn't look the page up. Nothing was changed.

**How to fix**

1. Open Manual from the navigation menu and find the page with the Search manual box or the page list. Links the Manual creates itself always use a valid page name.
2. If you copied the link from somewhere, check it wasn't cut off or changed. Page names use only lowercase letters, numbers and dashes. Capital letters, spaces or other symbols make the page name invalid.
3. If every Manual page fails to open, tell the person who manages SMTO. A damaged Manual installation, for example two pages with the same name, stops the Manual from loading its pages.

**What success looks like**

The page opens, and its link shows a page name made only of lowercase letters, numbers and dashes.

**If it still fails**

Copy the link and the error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit the Manual's files yourself to fix it.

**Technical details**

Manual ID validation failed: the requested document ID is not 1-120 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens starting with a letter or digit (HTTP 400), or corpus construction rejected duplicate document IDs, an unknown authority, inconsistent source classification or headings, or duplicate section references.

For a 400 response, use a valid lowercase document ID from GET /api/manual/catalog. If corpus construction raised ValueError in manual.corpus._snapshot, repair or reinstall the installed Manual content so document IDs and section references are unique and front-matter headings match the document body.
